claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is equiatomic.
Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi lowers the stacking-fault energy of the resulting FeNiCrMn alloy.
The lower stacking-fault energy enhances dislocation cross-slip.
The lower stacking-fault energy enhances dynamic recovery during deformation.
Modified dislocation behavior enables the Co-free alloy to retain a favorable strength–ductility balance over varied temperatures and strain rates relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
Arc melting followed by homogenization produces a single-phase solid-solution initial microstructure for the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy.
Removing Co alters electronic and atomic interactions in the solid solution.
Enhanced cross-slip and accelerated dynamic recovery allow the alloy to accommodate higher plastic strains with less localized strain-hardening failure.
Under varied temperature and strain-rate conditions, the proposed mechanism maintains or improves the strength–ductility balance relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
The Co-free alloy will show higher work-hardening rates than CoCrFeMnNi at intermediate temperatures and moderate strain rates.
The Co-free alloy will retain more ductility than CoCrFeMnNi at intermediate temperatures and moderate strain rates.
At approximately 200°C and 0.1 s^-1, the Co-free alloy will exhibit a more gradual yield drop than CoCrFeMnNi.
At approximately 200°C and 0.1 s^-1, the Co-free alloy will exhibit a higher strain to failure than CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to single-phase solid-solution high-entropy alloys below 500°C and from quasi-static through moderate dynamic strain rates.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply at extreme temperatures where phase transformations occur.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply at very high strain rates where inertial effects dominate.
Identically processing and testing the two alloys is intended to isolate the presence or absence of Co as the controlled compositional difference.
TEM-observed cross-slip and dynamic-recovery structures should differ between the Co-free alloy and the Co-containing baseline.
